sections.content: How many people stayed in Bolton after gaining qualifications?

Bolton is a large town in the North West. Bolton also has a university.

Bolton has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Bolton ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 9,425 state-school pupils from Bolton who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 2,995 (32%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 2,870 (30%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Bolton to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Bolton's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Bolton in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Bolton move to?

Of Bolton's graduates, 780 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 280 of those graduates (36%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Bolton's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 600 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 350 of those qualified non-graduates (58%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Bolton's GCSE cohort:

  • 355 graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 130 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North West
  • the most common regions they moved to were London and Yorkshire and The Humber

In 2018 to 2019, 18% of graduates and 19% of qualified non-graduates living in Bolton had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 2,660 graduates and 2,745 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Bolton. This is compared with the 2,995 graduates and 2,870 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 82% of the graduates had also lived in Bolton as GCSE pupils, while 18% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Bolton in 2018 to 2019, 81% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 19% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
